messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool eu-west-1 (dp-23) reporting p99 > 4s, queue depth rising past 900, and streaming stalls across chat-7b-v2. Autoscaler provisioning observed but handshakes failing. Paging on-call.

maya: I'm taking this. joining bridge now. any immediate customer-visible reports?

leo: yes — multiple clients reporting partial streams and aborted connections. p95 currently ~800ms but p99 spiking to ~4.3s starting ~10:11UTC. Router shows priority queue depth 940 at peak.

sam: autoscaler trace: provision request at 10:10:58; worker handshake attempts start but handshake timeouts happening repeatedly. New hosts boot, but model load/warmup for chat-7b-v2 is long (90-110s) due to full KV cache prime + quant init. while warming they can't accept streaming attachments.

emily: CS notes: 3 premium tenants flagged with degraded streaming sessions — total ~3.8% of requests aborted during the surge. Customers asking for timeline and mitigation steps. we've sent a brief alert that we're investigating and will reroute traffic.

ryan: root hypothesis: warmup + handshake gap. Hotshot pool drained under burst; autoscaler launched instances but they were unavailable for streaming until model fully loaded -> requests pinned to draining nodes -> queue amplification and tail latency blowout.

maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) shift VIP routes for affected tenants to eu-central-1 fallback pool with q4f quant variant, 2) enable stream-fallback mode for streaming clients to allow degraded-but-progressive token delivery, 3) increase prewarm for hotshot group by +2 nodes.

leo: deploying route swap now for tenants acct-101, acct-202. route command:
```
POST /routing/overrides
{ "from_pool": "dp-23", "to_pool": "eu-central-1-q", "tenants": ["acct-101","acct-202"] }
```

sam: autoscaler log snippet 10:10-10:16:
```
[10:10:58] provision_request pool=dp-23 want=3
[10:11:00] handshake_start worker=a1f4
[10:11:45] handshake_timeout worker=a1f4 -> retry
[10:11:46] handshake_start worker=b9c2
[10:13:20] model_load_begin worker=b9c2
[10:14:52] model_loaded worker=b9c2 duration=92s
```

ryan: note model_load duration ~92s. router currently pins streams to a target worker during handshake; if handshake takes > timeout, router retries but requests stay queued. we should change router to opportunistically route to warmed workers while new ones finish loading.

maya: doing two quick changes: reduce router pin time to 5s and enable opportunistic-fallback routing; also toggling stream-fallback feature flag for compatible clients. rolling these now.

emily: CS update sent at 10:19UTC: short note pointing to mitigation and giving ETA ~T+20m for full normalization. collecting logs from impacted tenants to attach.

leo: after initial reroute and fallback flip (10:20-10:23) we see immediate p99 drop in fallback pool; dp-23 queue depth down to 320. streaming abort rate down from 3.8% to 0.9%.

sam: manual prewarm request issued at 10:22 to add +2 hotshot nodes; also increasing autoscaler handshake timeout to 90s (was 45s) to avoid churn during heavy warmup loads.

ryan: precaution: while handshake timeout larger reduces churn, it can increase time requests wait for a genuinely failed worker — added logic suggested: mark worker as "warming" and exclude it from strict stream pinning until model_loaded event.

maya: checklist for live mitigation executed:
- reroute priority tenants to eu-central-1 fallback
- enable stream-fallback mode for streaming clients
- manual hotshot prewarm +2
- relax autoscaler handshake retries -> 90s
- enable opportunistic routing to warmed nodes

emily: customer comms: draft follow-up includes timeline, impact summary, and note that we'll publish postmortem and mitigation items within 48 hours.

leo: current telemetry (10:30UTC): dp-23 queue 160, p95 220ms, p99 610ms, streaming aborts ~0.4%. Stable but continue 30m watch. :thumbsup:

maya: handing to night on-call for observation window and post-incident cleanups. key follow-ups for postmortem:
- surface per-model warmup latency distribution into autoscaler decisions
- implement warmup-aware router pins (do not pin to workers marked warming)
- add prewarm reservation for streaming-heavy pools and burst buffer sizing
- add kv-prefetch metric and cold-path alerts

ryan: also recommend automating fallback quantized route for burst thresholds so routing fails over before queue > 300.

night-oncall: acknowledged. monitoring now. will escalate if p99 > 1s or queue > 250. grabbing traces for postmortem. thanks all for the handoff.
